heroHeadline: Ceasefire First Anniversary Eve: Pakistan Locks Down Islamabad, Chinese AVIC Engineers Reportedly Acknowledged May 2025 On-Ground Support; Pakistan Doctrine Pivots to Conventional Strike Depth
heroSubtitle: On May 9, 2026 — the eve of the first anniversary of the May 10, 2025 India-Pakistan ceasefire — Pakistan tightened security across Islamabad as the culmination of Pakistan's week-long Marka-e-Haq commemoration approached. Indian media reported that engineers from China's Aviation Industry Corporation (AVIC) publicly acknowledged on-ground technical support to Pakistan during the May 2025 conflict — a claim from a single Indian outlet not yet corroborated by major international outlets, but consistent with longstanding assessments of J-10C maintenance support. Defence analysis publication Quwa assessed that Pakistan is undergoing a significant doctrinal shift: pivoting from reliance on tactical nuclear deterrence (the Nasr/Hatf-IX doctrine) toward 'conventional strike depth' — deep-strike precision systems including the Taimoor cruise missile (600km range, tested January 2026), 40 ordered J-35A stealth fighters, and KJ-500 AWACS. Pakistan's official Marka-e-Haq anniversary documentary was released May 8 via state broadcaster Radio Pakistan, the fifth consecutive day of Pakistan's national anniversary information campaign. The IMF Board approved $1.32 billion in combined tranches for Pakistan on May 8, providing economic stabilization amid the post-conflict trade freeze. The ceasefire holds: bilateral freeze remains total — airspace closed until May 24, Indus Waters Treaty suspended, all direct trade halted, no ambassadors exchanged.
footerNote: Data sourced from Indian MEA/MOD, Pakistan ISPR/MFA, UN Security Council, SIPRI, Crisis Group, HRW, Stimson Center
